text:
Iris: FYI found a subtle correctness hole when combining prefix-gen demotes with async replication. sketch below.
Ken: hit me.
Iris: scenario: A has prefix P, writes W1 applied on A, async replicates to B slowly. During that window B wins ownership (fast takeover), becomes authoritative for new writes. A still serves reads from slab but without knowing B got W1, so stale reads.
Priya: seems like LSN visibility + demote ordering problem. gen handles demote->reader TOCTOU but not cross-node replication delays.
Vik: could we require takeover to include a min_lsn handshake: new owner only flips authoritative once it has lsn >= takeover_min_lsn. if new owner already has it, immediate. else wait or fallback.
Ken: that matches token idea we've floated. question: do we block handoff or make readers do safety checks?
Iris: tradeoffs: blocking takeover hurts rebalancing latency; reader-side checks add cheap compare but need per-entry lsn or slab-level watermark.
Priya: propose hybrid: token handshake to carry takeover_min_lsn, old owner marks handoff_in_progress and sets prefix.takeover_min_lsn. Readers consult slab.lsn(entry) vs takeover_min_lsn; if entry.lsn < takeover_min_lsn -> fallback_read(). New owner waits until applied_lsn >= takeover_min_lsn or timeout then flips.
Vik: need compact encoding for slab.lsn per-entry; add 32-bit LSN tag to entries (we already have small LSN tags for GC). cost minimal.
Ken: metrics: handoff.token_wait_ms, handoff.fallback_reads, handoff.forced_takeovers. ops-bot create canary?
ops-bot: created #CANARY-928: "takeover token handshake canary" assigned to @iris, due 2026-04-20 :white_check_mark:
Priya: corner: what if old owner is partitioned and never issues token? new owner must force takeover after timeout; we should log forced takeover and potentially mark windows of degraded correctness.
Iris: add audit events: takeover.requested, takeover.token_issued (min_lsn), takeover.applied, takeover.forced. those feed postmortem.
Vik: also combine with prefix.gen bump on demote so local stale-serving TOCTOU is mitigated. gen protects old-reader races; token protects cross-node replication races.
Ken: testing: microbench with asymmetric replication (drop some packets to B) and rapid churn. assert no stale reads when token protocol is used except when forced takeover occurred — those cases get logged.
Priya: add feature flag runtime.flags.takeover_token=true and canary rings. limit default timeout to 200ms and allow override per-ring.
Iris: implementation sketch done. will spike and push perf numbers. ETA next Tue.
Ken: also add a fast-path: if new owner already has applied_lsn >= proposed_min_lsl then it can flip without waiting; common in steady-state.
Vik: one more thought: fallback_read should be cheap (route to current authoritative node or read-through to backing store). prefer routing to new owner rather than full disk read.
Iris: agreed. fallback route = route_to(authoritative) which may be new owner. small extra hop.
Priya: sgtm. document the correctness invariant clearly: after takeover.applied, no read should return value with lsn < takeover_min_lsn for that prefix.
Ken: ok please file the RFC follow-up when you have numbers.
Iris: will do.
